findings.text: Requested page protections are filtered against static kernel reservations before use: non-present requests pass through unchanged, otherwise execution prohibition for kernel text, write prohibition for kernel text read-only and rodata, and execution prohibition for PCI BIOS overlap are accumulated and cleared from the request.

Region overlap is symmetric closed-interval intersection. Kernel text uses virtual address bounds, while PCI BIOS and rodata use frame-number bounds; rodata bounds derive from linker symbols with an exclusive end adjusted to an inclusive last frame, and BIOS enforcement additionally requires its enable flag while rodata enforcement requires read-only mode.

A full aligned large-page change skips the kernel-text read-only check as an optimization for callers that cover the whole large mapping; text read-only enforcement also only applies when read-only mode is active, the range overlaps text through aligned rodata, and the current translation is larger than a small page.

Conflict reporting is gated by a warning level and by whether the request retains a forbidden bit; each static-protection domain emits a distinct label and address plus frame plus requested versus prevented attributes when reporting.

Write-execute violation detection is bypassed on 32-bit, without hardware execution-disable support, when neither write nor execute-disable bits change, when the result is not writable plus executable, and for non-leaf entries that already restrict writing or execution; otherwise a one-time warning identifies old and new attributes plus range and frame, while still permitting the change.

Large-page handling supports only 2M and 1G levels and rejects other levels. It revalidates the entry pointer against a fresh lookup to detect races, clamps the requested page count to the remainder of the large page, derives base frame and base address, converts the current attributes to small-page format, applies caller clear and set masks, converts back to large-page format, normalizes protection-none encoding, and restores the large-page flag for present entries.

Large-page update returns preserve when requested attributes equal current attributes, split when coverage is partial or when existing or requested attributes disagree with static protections or write-execute validation, and an invalid argument for unsupported levels; an inconsistent existing mapping additionally arms forced static-protection repair during the later split.

Split decisions and split installation hold the page-table spin protection during lookup and entry replacement. The allocation path for a replacement table drops the change-attribute lock and optionally the initial address-space read lock around allocation, then reacquires them before proceeding.

Splitting copies the source large entry frame and normalized attributes into one entry per sub-page, with 1G splits advancing by medium-page stride and clearing the large-page flag when non-present, notifies paravirtual table allocation, installs the new table with kernel table protections, updates direct-map level accounting when the address is valid and mapped, and performs a global TLB flush before later attribute changes.

Fault handling for missing entries distinguishes a caller-supplied top-level table path that populates paging structures from identity-map holes that consume one page and synthesize its frame, highmap kernel-alias frames that fail silently, and other zero entries that warn and fail; non-primary paths consume one page without further action.

Population of a caller-supplied top-level entry allocates missing intermediate tables with kernel table protections, merges caller clear and set attribute masks into the table protection, delegates the lower-level fill, and on failure removes only the range just added while leaving the allocated intermediate page in place.

Address lookup honors an optional caller-supplied top-level base and otherwise uses the kernel top level; statistics hooks for checked, same-protection, and preserved large pages have counting and empty configurations.

Changing page size without a global flush can leave ordinary and large translations for the same range with undefined behavior, so a flush is required after installing a split table and before changing attributes. 32-bit additionally replicates entry updates across a global page-table list, and PUD static-protection repair cannot be fixed inline and only warns.
Shared page-table pages between kernel text and identity mappings in a paravirtual guest motivate bypassing text read-only enforcement when the current mapping already uses small pages.

Protection outcomes use execution-disable for text and BIOS reservations and write prohibition for text read-only and rodata reservations; large-page entries use a large-page flag when present, while global versus protection-none encoding is disambiguated for non-present entries.
Behavior distinguishes 4K, 2M, and 1G translation levels, three conflict reporting severities, and a kernel-table protection value used for newly installed paging-structure entries.
